_comment: CANONICAL CPS-1 romset table. This file is the single source of truth and
is checked into BOTH repositories byte-for-byte identically:
retro-go-sd     tools/cps1_romsets.json  -> generates cps1_romset.c
game-and-what   tools/cps1_romsets.json  -> drives upload validation
Neither side hand-edits its generated artifact. tests/test_cps1_romset_generated.sh
fails the build if cps1_romset.c is stale, and the sha256 of this file is
recorded in docs/CPS1_LIBRARY_CONTRACT.md so a divergent copy is detectable
from either side alone.
Transcribed from mamedev/mame src/mame/capcom/cps1.cpp ROM_START blocks.
The slot ORDER was independently re-derived from real dumps against the
assembled 4 MB GFX image the renderer draws a correct title screen from --
see linux/cps1/gfx_chips_selftest.c. It is data MAME owns; a new game means
reading its ROM_START, not inferring it.
prg: two 512 KB chips in ascending 68000 address order. prg[0] holds
0x000000-0x07FFFF and therefore the reset vector.
gfx: eight 512 KB chips in cps1_gfx_chip_byte() slot order -- slots 0-3 are
the 0x000000 half, slots 4-7 the 0x200000 half. NOTE that this is NOT
filename order: tk2_gfx3 is slot 1 and tk2_gfx2 is slot 2, and wofj's
upper chips are named tk205..tk208 which sort ahead of tk2_gfx1..4
entirely. Assigning by filename corrupts 85% of the region while every
file still loads and every size still checks out.
`parent` records MAME's cloneof relation. The firmware does not use it --
it matches on hashes alone -- but the library needs it to tell a user which
set to supply when a clone archive arrives on its own.
`filename` fields are COMMENTS. Nothing may look a chip up by them.

romsets.name: wofj
romsets.title: Tenchi wo Kurau II: Sekiheki no Tatakai (Japan 921031)

romsets.name: wofr1
romsets.title: Warriors of Fate (World 921002)
romsets._note: This is what the archive distributed as wof.zip actually contains: its program CRCs are wofr1's, not wof's. A zip's name does not describe its contents.

romsets.name: wof
romsets.title: Warriors of Fate (World 921031)
romsets._note: No dump of this set has been seen by this port. The entry costs 40 bytes and means a user who has one is not told their complete romset is unrecognised.
